channel.title: NorthEast News
channel.description: Clear, fast reporting for New Hampshire and New England.

item.title: Loudon Pentagon survivor marks 25 years since September 11
item.description: Retired public-affairs officer John Donovan is preserving memories of colleagues lost at the Pentagon and contributing to a forthcoming survivor history.

item.title: Concord library receives book overdue by more than 132 years
item.description: A Barrington man returned an 1894 magazine after spotting the library’s year-long fine freeze; archivists hope to display it in the Concord Room.

item.title: Oak Bluffs police search state barracks in sexual-assault investigation
item.description: Local officers executed court-authorized warrants at the Martha’s Vineyard facility while investigating an August report involving two people unaffiliated with State Police.

item.title: Jurors describe split that produced Lindsay Clancy mistrial
item.description: Five panel members have spoken publicly after a week of deliberations failed to produce a unanimous decision on criminal responsibility.

item.title: Rhode Island communities hold September 11 remembrance ceremonies
item.description: Observances across the state mark the attacks’ 25th anniversary with memorial services, wreath-laying and tributes led by public-safety agencies.

item.title: REGENT seaglider completes first crewed flight on Narragansett Bay
item.description: The North Kingstown company’s Viceroy prototype carried two captains in a brief ground-effect flight that begins the final stage of sea trials.

item.title: Hong Kong court gives Tiananmen vigil leaders seven-year terms
item.description: Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung were sentenced under the national security law after convictions tied to a disbanded group’s pro-democracy activities.

item.title: Hormuz vessel traffic falls to seven transits, tracking data shows
item.description: Preliminary Kpler data recorded sharply fewer commercial crossings Thursday than the recent average as war and shipping restrictions squeeze a critical energy route.

item.title: China targets large-scale autonomous-vehicle deployment by 2030
item.description: A new industry roadmap calls for self-driving systems on highways, urban expressways and selected city roads while tightening safety and software rules.

item.title: Microsoft plans to triple data-center capacity by 2032, report says
item.description: Bloomberg reported a target of roughly 38 gigawatts, with about one-third expected to support AI-specific chips; Microsoft did not immediately comment.

item.title: JetBlue raises seat-revenue outlook as fuel and disruption costs climb

item.title: Enflame shares triple in Shanghai debut after $912 million IPO
item.description: The Tencent-backed AI-chip company opened far above its offer price as investors continued to favor domestic semiconductor listings.

item.title: Rybakina rallies past Gauff to reach U.S. Open final
item.description: The incoming world No. 1 recovered from a set down for a 3-6, 6-4, 6-4 semifinal victory and will face defending champion Aryna Sabalenka.

item.title: Anthony Volpe returns with grand slam as Yankees sweep Rockies

item.title: Epsom water district staffing crisis stalls PFAS remediation
item.description: A one-member board and vacant administrative posts are delaying bids for a treatment project while the district weighs whether the town should assume control.

item.title: Kearsarge board targets two-school elementary model by summer 2028
item.description: The regional school board recommends closing Simonds Elementary and Sutton Central as part of a long-term consolidation plan, with local votes still required.

item.title: Capron Park Zoo mourns zookeeper Kayla St. George
item.description: The 39-year-old animal-care professional died after a stroke, leaving a record of work at several New England zoos and with a threatened deer species.

item.title: Judge keeps Wellesley mother held without bail in children’s deaths
item.description: A judge denied the defense request to release Janette MacAusland and dismiss the case while prosecutors await final medical-examiner findings.

item.title: Providence man charged after dog injured during police disturbance
item.description: Police arrested a 47-year-old man after an armed disturbance on Douglas Avenue; an injured dog was taken for veterinary treatment.

item.title: Rhode Island Blood Center urges donors during childhood cancer campaign
item.description: The center says many young cancer patients depend on blood components and is promoting a September 14 community drive in Warwick.

item.title: Russian strikes injure two and ignite Kyiv apartment fire, officials say
item.description: Kyiv authorities reported a fire in a nine-story residential building after overnight air attacks, while Russia’s Saratov region reported infrastructure damage.

item.title: Generator failures deepen power crisis at Gaza hospitals
item.description: Engine-oil and spare-parts shortages are forcing medical facilities to ration generator power while aid groups warn that essential services are at risk.

item.title: California enacts new child safeguards for social media and AI toys
item.description: A 13-bill package restricts addictive platform features for users under 16, bars AI companion toys for four years and expands protections against synthetic abuse material.

item.title: Micron’s Taiwan workers receive rewards worth up to 68 months of pay
item.description: The chipmaker announced large fiscal-year compensation packages for direct labor employees after unions showed strong support for possible strike action.

item.title: Global bond yields surge as oil shock revives rate-hike bets
item.description: Government debt sold off and Asian equities fell after rising energy prices and U.S. producer inflation pushed investors toward tighter-rate expectations.

item.title: Oil benchmarks head for first Fri, 11 Sep 2026 02:42:00 GMT 00-plus weekly finish since May
item.description: Brent and U.S. crude extended gains after shipping and supply disruptions, while OPEC again lowered its 2026 demand-growth forecast.

item.title: Sabalenka beats Pegula to reach fourth straight U.S. Open final
item.description: The world No. 1 advanced 7-5, 6-2 and will play for a third consecutive title at Flushing Meadows.

item.title: LIV Golf wins interim access to Fri, 11 Sep 2026 02:42:00 GMT 4 million in bankruptcy financing
item.description: A New Jersey court approved first-day Chapter 11 relief that lets the golf circuit continue paying employees and vendors while it reorganizes.

item.title: Chester delays Buxton Farm housing hearing for PFAS review
item.description: The Planning Board moved its review of a proposed 34-home rental community to September 30 while engineers finish environmental and plan reviews.

item.title: Springworks lettuce disappears from Hannaford as farm status remains unclear
item.description: The Maine aquaponics grower that supplied organic romaine across Hannaford’s footprint has stopped appearing on store shelves, with its business status unresolved.

item.title: Jennifer Hudson encourages young performers at Charlestown club
item.description: The singer and talk-show host met Boys & Girls Club members, answered questions and shared advice with young people interested in music.

item.title: Massachusetts trooper’s Quincy assault arraignment deferred to October
item.description: Christopher Regan is accused of punching another off-duty trooper at a Quincy bar; the charge remains an allegation and the case has not been decided.

item.title: Cranston West students plant 2,977 flags for September 11 victims

item.title: Manville volunteers prepare back-to-school clothes for local children
item.description: The Manville Share Shack and Pretty Cares are sorting donated clothing for a free community distribution planned for next weekend.

item.title: Two killed, seven injured in Belgorod drone attacks, officials say
item.description: Regional authorities reported fatalities in Novy Oskol and Shebekino as attacks continued across Russia’s border region.

item.title: First Circuit keeps block on new USPS mail-ballot rule

item.title: Pentagon discusses $5 billion Fluidstack loan, WSJ reports
item.description: The proposed financing would support domestic production of data-center components as Washington treats AI infrastructure as a strategic supply-chain priority.

item.title: Adobe revenue beats estimates as AI-first recurring sales double

item.title: American Eagle shares slide on flat margin outlook and core-brand weakness
item.description: The retailer kept its annual comparable-sales forecast after a revenue beat, but discounting and excess inventory continued to weigh on expectations.

item.title: Japan wholesale inflation holds at 7.6% before Bank of Japan meeting
item.description: Producer prices stayed above forecasts in August, reinforcing expectations that the central bank could raise its policy rate next week.

item.title: Flag relay begins 228-mile journey from Boston to Ground Zero

item.title: Infantino opponents shift toward FIFA governance reform as challenge falters
item.description: Reuters sources say the FIFA president retains enough association support to survive the challenge, pushing critics to focus on checks on executive power.

item.title: Federal Justice Department tells New Hampshire to retain 2024 ballots
item.description: The state says the request cites unspecified litigation and provides no factual or legal basis for suggesting New Hampshire violated election law.

item.title: New Hampshire election monitors report smooth state primary

item.title: Second suspect charged with murder in Taunton party shooting

item.title: Algeria cuts diplomatic ties with United Arab Emirates
item.description: Algiers cited unspecified hostile actions, while the UAE said it hoped the rupture would be temporary.

item.title: Jean Smart and Harrison Ford approach Emmy milestones

item.description: A new WMUR retrospective reunites members of the Hogs and looks back at a muddy football tradition rooted in North Conway.

item.description: A U.S. official told Reuters that an A-10 lost a wing and about eight F-15s sustained light damage during this week’s attack.

item.description: The fund said the world economy has absorbed the energy shock better than feared, while elevated prices and near-record public debt remain concerns.

item.description: Police say a southbound vehicle hit a stone wall and utility pole before catching fire near Linden Park early Thursday.

item.description: Digital-rights organization D3 says infinite scrolling, autoplay and personalized recommendations create harmful feedback loops.

item.description: AAA figures cited Wednesday put regular gasoline near a seasonal record, while higher crude prices renewed concern about diesel, heating oil and transportation costs.
